output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses most likely traces to the 12 August move of the alarm relay server, not to agency nurses. The new server loaded only 3 of its 14 forwarding rules. The import tool skipped the other 11 and still reported success. Those skipped rules held back brief SpO2 dips, suppressed repeat alerts, and sent probe-off alarms only to the charge phone. Since then, nurses in Pods A–C get about twice as many phone alerts per shift (about 80 versus 38), and acknowledgement time has doubled. Pod D was left on the old server and shows no change. In Pods A–C, core nurses, agency nurses and new graduates all show similar incident rates, so the agency share and staff experience don't explain it. Bedside alarm volume was flat, so acuity and the September monitor update don't explain it either. I'm less sure about the link to sick leave, and about the reports of phones not ringing in room 14. Don't approve the agency cap or the performance reviews. Don't switch off phone forwarding. Do restore the rules with Clinical Engineering validation, then track phone alerts per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Check room 14 separately.
